Terry Devlin scored his first Northern Ireland goal against Ukraine

It was a moment that Northern Ireland needed.

When Terry Devlin picked the ball up on the edge of the area in the 68th minute against Ukraine there was only one thought in his mind.

And when the ball flew into the corner Windsor Park erupted at another highlight of a Nations League campaign that has been a real feel-good story so far.

Heading into Saturday's game they had yet to concede a goal, but the one thing they had lacked was a home win - or even a home goal - after drawing blanks in stalemates with Hungary and Georgia in Belfast.

They had already come close when Jamie Donley slotted home in the first half but the forward had strayed offside, leaving the moment the hosts had been waiting for to come through Devlin's superb winner.

It leaves Northern Ireland's Nations League fate in their own hands, and a draw or better in Hungary would secure promotion to League A for the first time.

For Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill, it was a huge moment from a player who he said is "a bit of a dream" to manage.

"Terry's a great lad. He deserves everything he'll get from the game and he's one of those lads that maximises what he has," O'Neill said about the 23-year-old Portsmouth defender.

Northern Ireland beat Ukraine to move closer to Nations League promotion

Devlin nets winner as NI top Nations League group

Speaking about his versatility - Devlin can play in midfield as well as a full-back on either side - O'Neill added: "He does it with no fuss. He tries to do it to the best of his ability.

"He's a bit of a dream for a manager and he has the ability to contribute goals."

The average age of O'Neill's starting XI on Saturday was just 22.9 with eight players aged 23 or younger.

Devlin epitomises what this team are all about with his all-action display rewarded with a first international goal.

A versatile option, he broke through into senior football with his hometown club Dungannon Swifts in the Irish Premiership and impressive performances for Glentoran saw him earn a move to Portsmouth in 2023.

He has now become a cult hero at Fratton Park, and he is the club's top scorer in the Championship this season.

His winner in Belfast was a fitting moment for a player who continues to grow on the international stage.

"He's a very valuable player for Portsmouth and I think he's in the process of signing a new contract there, and I imagine a lot of teams in the Championship will be disappointed by that."

While Devlin will get the headlines after his man-of-the-match performance, goalkeeper Pierce Charles came up with a big moment of his own with a superb reflex save to deny Danylo Sikan in the closing stages.

The 21-year-old has yet to concede in the Nations League campaign, and he has produced several big moments to make it 466 minutes and counting without shipping a goal for Northern Ireland.

In front of him, the trio of Ruairi McConville, Tom Atcheson and Ciaron Brown were again rock solid.

"You don't keep five clean sheets because you're good with the ball at your feet. You keep five clean sheets because you make good decisions," O'Neill said on Charles.

"You make saves when it's needed. He kind of does it without any fuss as well, which I think is really good.

"He doesn't come and cause any issues with the back-three, which is very important for any goalkeeper, and he has a good decision-making process and a good understanding of the game."

Northern Ireland will now head to Hungary with their Nations League destiny in their own hands in what is essentially a Group B2 decider.

They are guaranteed a promotion play-off at the very least, but the goal will be to earn automatic elevation to League A for the first time.

Highlights: Devlin nets first international goal to seal victory

Considering Northern Ireland had just one Nations League win in 16 League B matches before the campaign, back-to-back promotions would be a remarkable achievement.

One down side from the win over Ukraine was the two yellow cards accumulated, one for O'Neill and the other for key striker Jamie Donley.

Both were for reactions to a perceived lack of decisions from French referee Francois Letexier, and both manager and player will now watch the game in Budapest from the stands.

"The referee doesn't like my reaction and there's not much I can do about that," O'Neill said.

"I would assume that I'm going to have to watch the game from the stands, but I'll be able to influence it from there, I'm sure."

On Donley's booking, which came for protesting after Letexier failed to stop play when Trai Hume was bleeding from a cut on his head, O'Neill said it was a "poor yellow".

"I thought Jamie had a very good game for us. He'll be a blow for us," he said.

Terry Devlin started his professional career in the Irish Premiership

But the suspensions will do little to dampen what was another encouraging night at Windsor Park.

Hungary had piled the pressure on Northern Ireland by winning in Georgia earlier on Saturday, and Northern Ireland's response sets up a showdown to top the group on Tuesday.

"We were aware that Hungary had won the game earlier and we're in a great position," O'Neill added.

"It would be great to win the group. It will be a tough, tough game but this is a brilliant game for us. It's a great arena to play in."

Having kept five clean sheets in as many matches, O'Neill is targeting completing the campaign without conceding.

If they can do that, they would not only win promotion but secure a play-off for Euro 2028 as a back-up should their qualifying group not go to plan.

"For a nation of our size, with our players at this stage of their careers, to have a chance to win the group and also to be playing Nations League A is a big achievement.

"I think we would probably be one of the smaller nations to play at Nations League A level since the start of the competition.

"We want to try to achieve that and we have a chance to do that on Tuesday night."

MN202611_1fub88j35n5.t:
Hallgrimsson's side sit third in Group B3 before their final game

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson says their 1-0 defeat by Austria in their penultimate Nations League game was "painful".

Substitute Sasa Kalajdzic poked home the winner in Linz, with the narrow victory ensuring Austria claimed top spot and automatic promotion to League A.

Chiedozie Ogbene squandered a late chance to equalise for the Republic and Hallgrimsson was frustrated they left the Raiffeisen Arena empty-handed when they had chances to secure the win which would have kept their hopes of winning the group alive.

"It was painful not to get anything from this match. I think we deserved at least a draw, but we needed the win for this game to count," he told RTE.

"I think we had the chances, the openings and the positions to do that, but this was not our day in goalscoring, so it is disappointing.

"Everything that we asked the players to do, they did and I think they gave everything.

"For that reason, we should be happy in a way but, obviously, we don't want to be building something, we want to win games."

Austria seal top spot with win over Republic of Ireland

Saturday's defeat left Hallgrimsson's side third in Group B3, a point behind Kosovo, who they face in their final game in Dublin on Tuesday.

Hallgrimsson was left to rue Republic of Ireland's inability to clear the corner from which Kalajdzic scored.

"We actually did have a lot of chances from that second ball in the box but it kind of never fell for our players in a good position," he added.

"They have a corner that they score from on the second or third touch. That's the game at this level. You need to be switched on and focused every second of the game."

Picking up a second win in the group against Kosovo would secure second place in the group which brings with it a promotion play-off and a move up to pot two for next month's Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

The Irish fell to a 1-0 defeat in Pristina in September and Hallgrimsson needs his side to finish strongly at home and pick up a vital three points.

"It was always that [Kosovo] game that was more important, but we were just so close to winning this one and being able to win the group but this is football at this level, it is all down to details."

Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023

Warning - this story contains graphic content

A woman who alleges that she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity and is campaigning for a staggered age of consent in an interview with the Sunday Times.

Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. She was known under the pseudonym 'Alice'. Brand denied the allegations at the time.

None of the women in the 2023 media investigation were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.

Reacting to the proposal, Cabinet Office Minister Louise Haigh said it would be a "massive step" to change the age of consent law, but that it "deserves proper consideration and scrutiny".

Speaking to the Sunday Times, she added that it was "disgusting" that a culture existed in the 2000s that "normalised and celebrated" celebrities having relationships with teenagers.

On Monday the entertainer was sentenced to 10 and a half years for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.

The Sunday Times reported that Latter had initially described the allegation about Brand to them as a sexual assault and that is how they reported it in their 2023 investigation.

Latter, 37, "now calls this allegation rape", the paper said.

Latter said she was 16 when she met Brand, who was 30 at the time, when she was on her way home from a shopping trip. She said Brand was working at MTV.

She told the paper: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power]."

She said Brand told her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends and claimed that he referred to her as "the child" in front of his entourage.

It was towards the end of their relationship that Latter was allegedly orally raped by Brand, according to the Sunday Times.

Latter said that she was now campaigning for the introduction of a "staggered" age of consent that would prohibit relationships between 16- and 17-year-olds and adults.

"I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other," she told the paper. "If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to. But … if you're in your thirties, forties and fifties and you're trying to have a relationship with someone under the age of 18, it [should be] a criminal offence."

She also told the paper that she would not continue with the criminal process so she could focus on her campaign.

In her interview with the Sunday Times she said that the CPS decided not to include her as part of Brand's criminal trial but the police wanted her to be part of a "subsequent trial".

A Met Police spokesperson said: "Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.

"Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.

"This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence."

A spokesperson for the Crown Prosecution Service said it would "continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible".

The Port of New Orleans is suing the owners and managers of a tanker that crashed into a cruise ship docked there on Friday.

The port is claiming the tanker is at fault for the collision that saw more than 100 passengers being rescued from the Mississippi River and caused more than $1m (£756,000) in damage, according to court documents.

The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one was unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi".

The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering."

The paddlewheel cruise ship, American Heritage, was left on its side and partially submerged in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt on Friday afternoon.

The court documents added that the port terminal had been "significantly damaged" in the incident.

The tanker, the M/V Atlantic Asphalt, its owner Nave Shipping SA and its management company Thome Ship Management Pte Ltd are all named in the lawsuit filed in federal court on Friday in the Eastern District of Louisiana.

Officials are still investigating the full extent of the damage from the crash, as well as the cause, but the lawsuit says the port is looking for money to cover clean-up, inspections, repairs and other expenses.

Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans

The lawsuit requests that the tanker be seized and sold to pay for the damage. It also alleges that the collision "occurred as a result of the negligence, gross negligence, fault or carelessness" of the ship and operating companies.

It alleges that the tanker and companies failed "to use all available means to avoid the risk" of colliding with the riverboat.

Nave Shipping is a subsidiary of the China State Shipbuilding Corporation. BBC has contacted the latter for comment.

Thome Ship Management has also been contacted. The firm said in a statement on Saturday that the crew of the Atlantic Asphalt were safe and accounted for.

"OSM Thome is fully complying with the local authorities as they carry out the necessary investigations," it said.

There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.

Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.

The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway at the time.

SpaceX has successfully caught the top part of its huge Starship rocket on its return to Earth for the first time.

"Can you believe it?," a commentator said as large crowds cheered at the launch site in Texas.

The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower.

But the first catch of the rocket's booster was aborted a few minutes after the launch on Friday. The booster was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames just above the sea.

The top part, known as the Ship, returned to Earth a few minutes behind schedule at around 15:20 local time (21:20 GMT) on Saturday, in the first-ever successful catch attempt.
